Busy. Thursday {homeLead}'s Club has the kitchen, so on Saturday I find their big pots in my pantry boxes. Every week. I don't complain. I put them back.

line: Nobody voted, if that's what you mean. But when the boiler broke he fixed it himself, and when the Garcías were short on rent the Club had it by Sunday. So people ask {homeLead} first. $ [guarded] He doesn't like the library people coming in with their flyers. I tell him, they bring apples. He says, we have apples.

3B! Sit, sit. I have twenty minutes for lunch and then back to work.
choice1: Mind if I sit a minute?

line: The hospital laundry, one floor under the ground, no windows. Nineteen years. So I come here and look at trees like a retired lady.
choice1: Nineteen years is a long time.
choice2: I'll let you enjoy the trees.

line: I started folding. Now I'm the supervisor, eleven people, two shifts. Some from Guatemala, two from the Philippines, one from Ohio. Mostly we talk about TV.
choice1: How did you learn the job?

line: When I started I had maybe twenty words of English. A lady from Manila trained me with her hands. Point, fold, point. Now I train the new ones the same way, whatever language they have.
choice1: That's a good way to learn.
choice2: I'll let you finish your lunch.

line: 3B, good, you're here. Can I ask you something? It's about Daniel's college.
They sent a letter about his financial aid. Four pages. I read it three times. Will you look at it with me?
choice2: I'm not good with those either.
choice3: Can we do it another day?

line: Page two says 'verification.' They want his father's tax return. Héctor files every year. But the copy is in a box somewhere since we moved.
choice1: The IRS can send a transcript.

line: Don Ernesto does Héctor's taxes every year. He keeps copies of everything, in folders, with labels. I'll ask him Saturday. He'll give me the speech about shoeboxes.

line: You see? This is why I ask you. Daniel would say 'Mamá, I'll do it,' and then it's April. He's the first one in the family at a college here, and every letter they send, I feel like they're checking me, not him.

line: Okay. Tonight I find the box. You come for coffee Sunday, and you read page three, because page three I didn't understand at all.

line: Hi, 3B. Sorry, I'm a little distracted today.
Héctor drives the number 6 bus. Yesterday two men got on at Fifth and asked a passenger for his papers. Héctor had to keep driving.

line: He didn't sleep. He says it's not his business, he drives the bus. But he knows the man. Every morning at Fifth, with his lunch in a plastic bag.
They took him off at the next stop. This morning Héctor left early to look for the man's wife at Fifth. I said, and tell her what? He went anyway.

line: 3B. Come in a minute. You heard about Rodrigo? Rodrigo Salas, from the eight o'clock Mass. $ They stopped him at the checkpoint by the Fifth Street bridge, on his way to the warehouse. He didn't come home.

His wife called {homeLead} at six in the morning. By nine {homeLead} had her at legal aid on Fifth, and by noon the library had know-your-rights cards at the front desk, both languages. $ She says the whole town should see what this does to a family. Not only us.

line: His wife called {homeLead} before she called the priest. The Club's lawyer was on the phone before Mass was over. The fund pays, he says, nobody has to beg the city. $ [guarded] And he told the young men, stay off the bridge, go the long way, and don't talk to anybody with a clipboard.

line: They moved him to the detention center, two hours from here. Sunday the priest read his name, and the ladies made a list of meals for his wife and the two boys. The list was full before the coffee was.

Bring something Thursday, anything that keeps. Rice, a cake, it doesn't matter. Héctor is driving her to the center on his day off. $ [guarded] And 3B. Carry your ID when you go to work. I know, I know. Carry it anyway.

line: 3B! Come here, look at this.
Ana's school sent a letter in Spanish and English. Side by side, same page. Twenty years I've been reading those letters with a dictionary.
No, now I read English fine. But Héctor read this one. He never reads the school letters. He says the school is my department.
Twenty years, yes. Conferences, forms, everything. Last night he read it at the table and asked Ana about her science grade. She looked at me like, who is this man?
Every time I'm at the hall, you're there. Good.

line: When I came, I didn't go to the hall for two years. I was working, and I thought, I'm here now, I do things like here. Then Daniel had a fever at midnight and I needed somebody to tell me what to do, in Spanish.
So I went. Pilar's mother came to the emergency room with me and sat there until six. Now when somebody new comes to the pantry, I'm the one who sits.

line: 3B. I haven't seen you at the hall in a while.

Everything, more or less. She got an A. So the library is fine, go. Just come on Saturday sometimes too.
Oh. Hello, 3B.
choice1: I'm sorry I was short with you before.

line: Okay. I was busy that day too. The shower is still dripping, by the way.
Not now, I'm counting cans. Forty-one beans, nine tomato. Somebody gave us cranberry sauce in October.
